styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small purple office chair of about one tile, drawn with only 8 colours in total. That is about 3 steps per material: a light purple seat and back, a mid tone, a dark tone, and dark legs. The bench reference has 14 colours and about 4-5 wood steps with visible grain and plank edges. The measured facts show 8 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge, so density is comparable only to the sparsest reference. It is well below the stall (17) and the well (20). The outline is tinted dark purple, not neutral (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels), so it avoids the black-sticker look. Near-flat coverage is 0%, but only because the object is tiny. By eye the seat and back are mostly smooth fills with no texture dots, grain or per-part highlights, so the chair looks flatter and thinner than the bench. When in doubt, fail.
